newsitem.title: USA: SEC approves AMEX smaller increments trading plan.
newsitem.headline: SEC approves AMEX smaller increments trading plan.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday it has approved the American Stock Exchange's plan to allow stocks on the exchange to trade in smaller increments.
That means that, beginning Wednesday, stocks on the exchange can trade in minimum increments of 6.25 cents rather than 12.5 cents.

"Smaller trading increments mean greater opportunity for improved prices when buying and selling stocks," said Exchange Chairman Richard Syron. "We're pleased to be leading the way in an effort that directly benefits all investors and our listed companies."
The changes will allow all AMEX-listed stocks priced at or above 25 cents to trade in increments as small as one-sixteenth of a dollar or 6.25 cents.

Prior to this rule change, AMEX-listed securities whose price was equal to or greater than $10 could only trade in eighths and only those priced between 25 cents and $10 could trade in sixteenths. Now, all securities listed on the exchange that trade at 25 cents or higher can trade in the smaller increment.

Approval of the AMEX plan comes at a crucial time as lawmakers on the House Commerce Committee are considering a measure that would move stock quoting in the United States to dollars and cents from fractions.

That bill was introduced by Representative Michael Oxley, an Ohio Republican who chairs the Finance Subcommittee and Representative Edward Markey, a Massachusetts Democrat who is a key member of the committee.

Supporters of the measure say a shift to decimals from fraction trading would enable investors to save money in transaction costs because there would be a narrowed difference between the prices at which they buy and sell stocks.
